Meeting Recap: 8/30/22

Modifications and Next Steps
I've attached Emilia's Reading progress report to this email. As a reminder, light blue boxes are levels already completed at her assessment, dark blue is anything completed since, and green is in progress. The red line is "on grade level" for the average 2nd grade student. Because of our emphasis on Vocab during the summer, Emilia bumped ahead faster in those exercises than comprehension. Based on the 30-40 hours per level recommendation, Emilia is right on track (in fact she's progressing a little on the fast side!)
Jen, you expressed your greatest concern was Emilia's writing. You said you couldn't help comparing her handwriting and letter formation to other students at Back to School Night and believe she's very behind. Her ideas are all there, and she has many creative stories, but getting the words and letters onto the page remain difficult. 2nd Grade is the perfect spot to start our TC Writing curriculum, so I will plan to get a writing sample from Emilia at our next couple of sessions and follow-up then with a writing progress report. In the meantime, since she's fairly close to her reading goal and reading is such an important foundation to writing, we will keep Emilia's 2 hours a week focused on TC Reading. If/when we add writing practice, it will be a third hour (see more below).
We briefly discussed that Emilia's Kindergarten was virtual, leading to less robust handwriting instruction. We also both loosely speculated about dysgraphia / dyslexia, and while I'm not in a position to make that diagnosis, we do have many reading instructional methods, students, and tutors who cope and work with both. 
You are more than welcome to give my contact info to Emilia's teacher / get her further recommendation on reading vs. writing focus
I have added Emilia to our Saturday waitlist each week of the fall semester. Right now our Saturdays are very full, but we're onboarding a few new tutors and expect wider availability soon. In the meantime, Sam or myself can email at the end of each week with hour options for the following  Saturday. You said Emilia's own Saturday availability changes, hence not wanting to take up a permanent spot on the schedule, but want to be aware of availability if and when we can fit her in this semester for that third hour a week.
Meeting Summary
Emilia just started 2nd grade at Haycock Elementary School. She is enjoying it so far and hit the ground running. Her teacher has a big emphasis on Phonics-Based Reading Instruction (which I love) Emilia is looking forward to the school year with her. Emilia already has the iReady, DRA, and CogAT coming up (yay standardized tests... 🎉) She's also reading for homework 20 minutes every night and enjoying it so far.
Since Emilia started at TC in January, she's attended about 60 hours. About 25 of them have been in her current TC Reading program (moved up from Beginning Reading.) Over the summer, based on feedback from school, we had a heavier focus on Vocabulary exercises and supplemental vocab activities to demonstrate mastery and application of new words whenever possible. She's worked with our Certified Reading Specialist Ms. Autumn whenever possible and continues to be on Ms. Autumn's schedule throughout the fall.
Related to the vocab focus, Jen, you noticed Emilia utilising a greater variety of words especially now at the beginning of the school year. You've also noticed increased stamina though Emilia is still hesitant to read out loud.
Emilia continues to love coming to TC (and our tutors continue to love working with her.) She loves the token system, enjoys engaging with tutors and other students at the table, and is becoming a more confident reader. She is occasionally grumpy about going to TC (especially if it's interrupting play time) but always cheerful by the time she comes out.
That makes sense to me, I think we all have days where heading to work or to school is more of a drag than we'd like. But I'm happy to hear Emilia always feels better once she's been in with us.

Next Steps and Modifications
The plan right now is to keep Molly in TC Writing 3 hrs/week to continue to catch up in proficiency. With Ellie, we'll continue 2 hours a week of TC Writing and build in TC Math to her third hour to maintain interest and proficiency in both areas.
As I mentioned, we recommend 2 hours a week to see progress in a given curriculum. So 1 hour of math is likely enough to 'hold Ellie over' alongside school, but to really move ahead we'd recommend a 4th hour when possible. We agreed you may be able to fit that in on occasion and will look for opportunities to also get Molly in for four hours so she can also try TC Math.
I know we're in the process of onboarding new tutors for Saturday so hopefully some more Saturday spots will open soon.
You also mentioned scheduling is a challenge (and I promise you're not the only ones.) It is completely fine to flex and reschedule sessions as needed, just reach out to SchedulingNVA@TutoringClub.com as soon as you know what will and won't work. As a reminder, we require at least 48 hours advance notice to excuse an hour, as otherwise we've locked in that tutor and student schedule.
You mentioned the girls like most of their tutors and enjoy TC, but have felt they receive less feedback from Mr. Joe and he's more likely to just transition them to the next thing without always going over everything. I'll be touching base with him this week and next as a training opportunity, and additionally I've moved Ellie and Molly off of Mr. Joe's schedule at least for right now, so they're paired with other tutors.
As I mentioned, as a younger guy Mr. Joe is popular with many of our middle school boys. But since he's less upbeat and more laidback, Molly and Ellie aren't the only 'more energized' students to not mesh as well with him. And that's completely alright :)
Meeting Summary
Ellie is starting 4th grade at Discover and Molly has started 6th grade at Williamsburg. So far so good, though they're still adjusting into classes and new expectations. I'm also glad to hear Ellie likes her teacher and her class at Discovery.
Ellie and Molly have each attended 48 hours of tutoring focused on our TC Writing curriculum. We usually estimate 30-40 hours to get through a given level of TC Writing, and both girls have been on track with that estimate. Ellie is now at a benchmark to be on-grade-level for a rising 4th grader; Molly remained further behind as she started with a larger gap and there is more of a curve to proficiency as TC Writing moves into middle school (Level G/H) and high school (Level I) levels.
Additionally, Molly and Ellie have received glowing tutor feedback. You said they love coming to TC and we love having them. They've made rapid progress through the curriculum, and actively showed you their writing compositions (especially at the beginning.) I've attached a couple rough or revised drafts from their notebooks here. Looking through Ellie's reminded me of how often she ends up writing about sloths when we work together 😆 Ellie continues to be more resistant to writing / likes it less, but as I mentioned on the phone my goal is never to force students to like writing, just to make it more approachable, less daunting, and lay the foundations for them.
I'm very glad to hear they both continue to be involved in soccer and were able to keep busy over the summer.
